Real defect: line 96 — `contactId` is read from cursor.getString(1) which is _ID column; then used in selection args for Phone/Email queries — fine. Real defect: line 131-135 — `result.success` is called inside the try block after the outer query's `.use{}`; if the outer query returns null (no cursor), the whole block silently skips and result.success is never called — the Dart future never completes. Actually line 90 `contentResolver.query(...)?.use { ... }` — if query returns null, the use block doesn't run, name stays null, and execution continues to line 131 result.success — no, the `?.use` returns null but execution continues past it since it's a statement, not a return. - [medium] android/app/src/main/kotlin/com/tiltastech/lineguide/PaddleOcrPlugin.kt:309-328 — `ocrImage` runs `cropBitmap` (a fresh `Bitmap.createBitmap` copy, line 425) plus a full `recognize` ONNX inference per detected box, sequentially, with no batching and no cap on box count — recognition is the measured 88% of page time (~95ms per line, per the in-code comment at 276–281); a dense page with hundreds of boxes yields hundreds of sequential ~95ms inferences — consequence: per-page wall time grows linearly (and unboundedly with box count) on the OCR worker thread; a 50-page PDF import can take minutes — smallest safe fix: batch crops through the rec model's dynamic batch dimension (padding-aware, as the reverted experiment noted) or at least sort/limit crops by confidence/area and early-exit on a caller-supplied max-lines bound. {mlx-performance-review@ds4-glm-5.3-flash-q2}

- [medium] android/app/src/main/kotlin/com/tiltastech/lineguide/PaddleOcrPlugin.kt:309-328 — recognize loop crops each detected box into a new Bitmap (cropBitmap → Bitmap.createBitmap) and runs a full ONNX inference per crop sequentially, with no batching and no cap on box count — trigger: every page OCR; growing input: number of detected boxes (unbounded by detMinBoxArea=16 on dense/noisy pages — hundreds possible); work per unit: one Bitmap.createBitmap + one rec ONNX run (~95ms measured) per box; affected resource: CPU + wall-clock on the OCR worker thread; consequence: page latency scales linearly with box count; a noisy page with 100+ boxes takes 10s+ and the whole ocrPdf job serializes over pageCount; smallest safe fix: cap crops per page (e.g. top-N by area/confidence or merge adjacent boxes) and/or batch crops through the rec model's dynamic batch dim with padding, which the comment says was tried but reverted — re-evaluate with correct padding instead of dropping the lever. {android-performance-review@ds4-glm-5.3-flash-q2}
- [medium] android/app/src/main/kotlin/com/tiltastech/lineguide/PaddleOcrPlugin.kt:309-328 — the recognition loop crops, runs ONNX, and decodes each box sequentially with no batching, and each iteration allocates a crop Bitmap, a tensor, and a StringBuilder — with hundreds of boxes on a dense page this is O(boxes) sequential model invocations on one worker thread — consequence: recognition dominates the per-page budget (measured ~3.8s at ~95ms/line) and scales linearly with box count, so a 100-line page takes ~10s and a multi-page PDF import blocks progress reporting for minutes — smallest safe fix: batch crops into the rec model's dynamic batch dimension with fixed-width padding (the comment says naive padding corrupted text, so pad to a fixed bucket width and mask), or at minimum reuse crop/tensor buffers across iterations. {kotlin-performance-review@ds4-glm-5.3-flash-q2}

- [low] integration_test/android_live_matching_test.dart:200 — chunk-walk advances `i += 8 + sz + (sz & 1)` even when `sz` is garbage (e.g. a non-WAV file whose bytes happen to parse) — can loop past `wav.length` only because the guard `i + 8 <= wav.length` re-checks each iteration, but a huge `sz` skips the `data` chunk entirely and the function returns an empty buffer with no error — same fix as above: validate the parsed header before use. {flutter-review@ds4-glm-5.3-flash-q2}
- [low] integration_test/android_live_matching_test.dart:200 — chunk-walk advances i by 8+sz+(sz&1) but never validates sz against remaining length; a corrupt/truncated wav header can make dataStart/dataLen point past EOF, and getInt16 at line 211-212 then throws RangeError mid-test — clamp dataLen to wav.length - dataStart before allocating out {ml-inference-pipeline-review@ds4-glm-5.3-flash-q2}
- [low] integration_test/android_live_matching_test.dart:200-201 — chunk-walk advances `i += 8 + sz + (sz & 1)` even when `id` is unrecognized, but for the `data` chunk it sets `dataStart`/`dataLen` and then continues walking past the data payload using `sz`, which is correct; however if `sz` is 0 (common for streamed WAVs with unknown length), `dataLen` becomes 0 and the resampler emits an empty buffer with no error — smallest safe fix: treat `dataLen == 0` as an explicit failure rather than producing silence. {observability-review@ds4-glm-5.3-flash-q2}

- [high] integration_test/android_rehearsal_harness_test.dart:99-104, 234-238, 252, 277-287 — sleep/duration-based synchronization everywhere — readiness is a 6-minute wall-clock polling loop, mic-open retry is a fixed 600 ms sleep, trailing-silence settle is a fixed 1500 ms sleep, and transcript settle is a 100 ms poll against a 30 s deadline; all of these are timing guesses that flake on slow emulators and mask real latency regressions (a slower engine just "passes" by burning the sleep). — consequence: intermittent false failures and false passes; the latency asserts at 142/161 measure stopwatch time but the surrounding waits are unmeasured, so a regression can hide inside the slack. — smallest safe fix: replace fixed sleeps with condition-based waits (poll the actual ready/complete futures with a bounded timeout, e.g. `Future.wait` on `lineDone.future` / `recording` state) and keep the sleeps only as trailing-silence audio content, not as synchronization. {testing-review@ds4-glm-5.3-flash-q2}

- [medium] integration_test/asr_streaming_macos_test.dart:86-104 — LCS matcher silently returns 0 on empty input — `_matchRate` returns 0 when `a.isEmpty || b.first.isEmpty` (line 93), which is indistinguishable in the printed output from a recognizer that produced garbage; a candidate whose transcript is empty scores 0% and the mean-match print (line 171) still divides by `_lines.length` without any floor assertion, so a totally broken recognizer can be reported as "mean match: 0%" and the test still passes. — consequence: the evaluation can pass with every candidate scoring zero; nothing fails. — smallest safe fix: add `expect(total / _lines.length, greaterThan(0.5))` (or per-line floor expects) after the loop so a degenerate recognizer fails the test. {testing-review@ds4-glm-5.3-flash-q2}
- [medium] integration_test/asr_streaming_macos_test.dart:86-104 — `_matchRate` implements LCS but the DP recurrence at 98-100 is wrong for the standard LCS: when characters differ it should take `max(prev[j], cur[j-1])` (i.e. `max` of the two neighbors), not the nested ternary `prev[j] > cur[j-1] ? prev[j] : cur[j-1]` evaluated against the *previous* row's `cur` slot; as written the recurrence can drop a legitimate match and under-report the match rate, so a recognizer that got most of the line right can be scored 0% and the test's `total`/mean assertions (167-172) silently pass/fail on a broken metric — smallest safe fix: replace the ternary with `max(prev[j], cur[j - 1])` (or use `math.max`) so the DP is the textbook LCS recurrence. {flutter-review@ds4-glm-5.3-flash-q2}
- [medium] integration_test/asr_streaming_macos_test.dart:86-104 — copy-pasted logic already diverged: `_matchRate` implements a word-level LCS DP but the recurrence at lines 98-100 (`cur[j] = a[i-1]==b[j-1] ? prev[j-1]+1 : (prev[j] > cur[j-1] ? prev[j] : cur[j-1])`) is a *length* recurrence, yet line 104 divides `prev[b.length]` by `a.length` and the doc comment claims "fraction of expected length" — the DP tracks LCS length correctly but the normalization silently treats a transcript *longer* than expected as full credit (e.g. hallucinated repeats score 1.0), unlike any precision/recall blend — either normalize by `max(a.length, b.length)` or compute precision and recall separately so over-generated transcripts cannot score 100%. {maintainability-review@ds4-glm-5.3-flash-q2}

Reachability: authenticated user analyzing their own recordings = medium per rubric, but consequence is bounded by file size the user controls; keeping at medium is defensible only if untrusted/large files can be passed — since path comes from the Dart side over the channel, an authenticated user controls it, so medium. {ios-performance-review@ds4-glm-5.3-flash-q2}

- [medium] ios/Runner/BackgroundDownloadPlugin.swift:67-75 — persistDownloadRecord rewrites the entire UserDefaults dictionary on every download start — trigger: each startDownload call; growing input: records dict grows with number of distinct models downloaded (unbounded, never pruned except on cancel/complete); work per unit: O(n) read + O(n) write of the whole plist blob per call; affected resource: UserDefaults plist I/O on the main thread (delegateQueue is .main, line 44, and handle runs on the platform channel main thread); consequence: with hundreds/thousands of downloaded models in the dict, each new download start serializes and deserializes the whole dictionary, adding main-thread latency to the UI method-call handler; smallest safe fix: store one UserDefaults key per modelId (`persistKey + "/" + modelId`) so persist/remove are O(1) writes, or move persistence off the main thread. {mlx-performance-review@ds4-glm-5.3-flash-q2}
- [medium] ios/Runner/BackgroundDownloadPlugin.swift:68-74, 77-82 — `UserDefaults` read-modify-write of the whole records dictionary is not atomic across plugin instances; two rapid `startDownload` calls from different isolates (or a relaunch replay racing a cancel) can lose a record — use one serialized mutation path or `UserDefaults` with a single object write under a lock. {ios-review@ds4-glm-5.3-flash-q2}
- [medium] ios/Runner/BackgroundDownloadPlugin.swift:68-75,77-82 — UserDefaults read-modify-write of the whole records dictionary from multiple call sites without any synchronization — concurrent startDownload/cancelDownload (or a delegate callback racing a method call) can drop a just-persisted record, so a completed post-relaunch download is silently discarded (the exact failure the persistence was added to prevent) — guard the read-modify-write with a serial queue/lock and route all record mutations through it. {crypto-security-review@ds4-glm-5.3-flash-q2}
- [medium] ios/Runner/BackgroundDownloadPlugin.swift:77-82 — removeDownloadRecord also rewrites the whole records dictionary per removal — trigger: every cancelDownload and every didFinishDownloadingTo completion; growing input: same unbounded records dict; work per unit: O(n) full read-modify-write; affected resource: UserDefaults plist I/O on main thread; consequence: completion/cancel of one download pays the cost of the entire download history; smallest safe fix: per-modelId UserDefaults key (delete just that key) instead of one shared dictionary blob. {ios-performance-review@ds4-glm-5.3-flash-q2}
- [medium] ios/Runner/BackgroundDownloadPlugin.swift:77-82 — removeDownloadRecord has the same whole-dictionary rewrite cost as persistDownloadRecord — trigger: every cancelDownload and every didFinishDownloadingTo completion; growing input: same unbounded records dict; work per unit: O(n) read-modify-write; affected resource: main-thread UserDefaults I/O; consequence: completion/cancel of many downloads pays growing plist serialization on the main thread; smallest safe fix: per-modelId UserDefaults keys (one finding, same root cause as line 67). {mlx-performance-review@ds4-glm-5.3-flash-q2}
- [low] ios/Runner/BackgroundDownloadPlugin.swift:93,155,171,182,199,218,284,287 — `NSLog` of modelId/URL/error strings into the unified system log — destination paths and URLs (which may embed signed query params or user-identifying slugs) persist in device logs readable by any app with log access on that device and in sysdiagnose dumps — log only the modelId hash/length and error domain/code, not full URLs or destination paths. {security-review@ds4-glm-5.3-flash-q2}
- [high] ios/Runner/BackgroundDownloadPlugin.swift:100-110 — `url` comes straight from the Dart side with no scheme/host validation; a malicious or compromised Dart layer (or a deep link that reaches this channel) can make the native side fetch `file://`, `http://` (cleartext), or arbitrary hosts and write the response to any `destinationPath` — validate scheme is `https` (or app-specified hosts) before building the task. {ios-review@ds4-glm-5.3-flash-q2}
- [medium] ios/Runner/BackgroundDownloadPlugin.swift:100-110 — no validation of caller-supplied `url`/`destinationPath` at the method-channel trust boundary — a Dart-side (or compromised plugin channel) caller can point the native downloader at arbitrary URLs (including internal/LAN hosts, i.e. SSRF from the app process) and write the downloaded bytes to any absolute path the app can reach (e.g. overwriting Documents/Library files or clobbering an existing file at a chosen path) — validate scheme/host allowlist for `url` and confine `destinationPath` under a fixed app container directory before creating directories or starting the task. {security-review@ds4-glm-5.3-flash-q2}
- [low] ios/Runner/BackgroundDownloadPlugin.swift:113-115 — `destDir` is derived by `deletingLastPathComponent` on the *destination file path* and created with `try?`, so a bad `destinationPath` (e.g. relative path with no directory component) silently skips directory creation and the later `moveItem` fails with "Failed to save file" — surface the FileManager error to Dart instead of `try?` at line 114-115, or validate that `destDir` is non-empty and absolute. {maintainability-review@ds4-glm-5.3-flash-q2}
- [low] ios/Runner/BackgroundDownloadPlugin.swift:113-115 — `try?` on `createDirectory` swallows directory-creation failure; the subsequent move at line 206 then fails with a confusing "Failed to save file" error instead of the real cause — log or surface the createDirectory error. {swift-review@ds4-glm-5.3-flash-q2}
- [low] ios/Runner/BackgroundDownloadPlugin.swift:113-115 — `try?` on createDirectory swallows directory-creation failure; the later moveItem at 206 then fails with "Failed to save file" and the multi-GB download is dropped after completion — surface the error or at least log it so the failure is diagnosable. {crypto-security-review@ds4-glm-5.3-flash-q2}
- [medium] ios/Runner/BackgroundDownloadPlugin.swift:113-115 — `destinationPath` is used unchecked to build directories and the final move target; a path with `..` traversal or an absolute path outside the app sandbox would still be honored by `FileManager` (sandbox limits actual escape, but in macOS-derivative or extension contexts it may not) — canonicalize and confine to the app's documents/container directory. {ios-review@ds4-glm-5.3-flash-q2}
- [medium] ios/Runner/BackgroundDownloadPlugin.swift:113-115 — `try?` swallows directory-creation failure and the code proceeds to start the download anyway — if the destination directory cannot be created (disk full, sandbox denial, bad path), the transfer completes and the move in `didFinishDownloadingTo` then fails, surfacing a generic "Failed to save file" error after a multi-GB download instead of failing fast — drop `try?`, return an error to the caller when `createDirectory` fails before scheduling the task. {security-review@ds4-glm-5.3-flash-q2}
- [medium] ios/Runner/BackgroundDownloadPlugin.swift:118-124 — `activeDownloads` is a value-type dictionary mutated through `var info` copies, so `retryCount` increments and task updates can be lost between call sites — e.g. `scheduleRetry` mutates a copy (line 168-180) and the asyncAfter closure re-copies again (line 184-186), while `didFinishDownloadingTo` reads a snapshot (line 198) — a retry racing a completion can resurrect a finished download or double-count retries — store `DownloadInfo` as a class (`final class DownloadInfo { ... }`) so all call sites share one mutable instance, or funnel every mutation through a single `update(modelId:)` helper. {maintainability-review@ds4-glm-5.3-flash-q2}
- [medium] ios/Runner/BackgroundDownloadPlugin.swift:118-125 — `startDownload` cancels an in-flight task but leaves its `DownloadInfo` in `activeDownloads` and its persisted record intact; the cancelled task's `didCompleteWithError` (NSURLErrorCancelled) is swallowed at line 270, so the new task's record is overwritten only by the immediately following `persistDownloadRecord` — but if the new task fails before the old one's cancel callback fires, `scheduleRetry` can resurrect a stale `DownloadInfo` whose `task` points at the cancelled task — clear the old record (memory + persisted) synchronously when cancelling, before creating the new one. {swift-review@ds4-glm-5.3-flash-q2}
- [medium] ios/Runner/BackgroundDownloadPlugin.swift:118-126 — `startDownload` cancels an in-flight task but never removes its persisted record before overwriting, and the cancelled task's `didCompleteWithError` (NSURLErrorCancelled) returns early at line 270 without clearing the resume blob — a stale `.resume` file from the old destination/URL can be picked up by `startTask` at line 153 for the new download, silently resuming a transfer from the wrong source — clear the resume file and persisted record when cancelling an existing task before starting the new one. {ios-review@ds4-glm-5.3-flash-q2}
- [medium] ios/Runner/BackgroundDownloadPlugin.swift:118-126 — cancel-then-start race with no state reconciliation: the old task is cancelled but its persisted record is immediately overwritten by `persistDownloadRecord(info)` for the new URL/destination — if the cancelled task's error callback (line 282-289) fires after the new record is written, `scheduleRetry`/resume-data handling runs against the *new* download's state, potentially writing the old task's resume data over the new download's blob and retrying the wrong transfer — key resume data and retry state by a per-task identifier (or remove the record before cancelling and re-add only after the old task's callbacks have drained). {security-review@ds4-glm-5.3-flash-q2}
- [medium] ios/Runner/BackgroundDownloadPlugin.swift:118-126 — startDownload cancels an in-flight task but leaves its persisted record and resume blob in place, then immediately overwrites the record — the cancelled task's didCompleteWithError fires with resume data and writes a stale resume blob for the new download's destination, so the "fresh" download can resume from a partial transfer of a different request — remove the record and resume blob before starting the new task (cancelDownload path at 134-141 already does this; mirror it here). {crypto-security-review@ds4-glm-5.3-flash-q2}
- [medium] ios/Runner/BackgroundDownloadPlugin.swift:118-126 — startDownload cancels an in-flight task but leaves its stale resume-data blob on disk; the new task then resumes from the old blob — a fresh download for the same modelId can silently continue a partial transfer of a *different* URL/destination, corrupting the file — delete `resumePath(destinationPath)` (and the old record) before `startTask`, same class as the cancel path at 138. {ml-inference-pipeline-review@ds4-glm-5.3-flash-q2}
- [medium] ios/Runner/BackgroundDownloadPlugin.swift:134-141 — `cancelDownload` only cancels when the task is in the in-memory `activeDownloads` map; a download that completed/failed while the app was terminated has no in-memory entry, so cancel silently succeeds (`result(true)`) without removing the persisted record or the resume blob — a later `startDownload` for the same modelId can then resume from stale resume data the user believed they had cancelled — call `removeDownloadRecord(modelId)` and delete `resumePath` unconditionally in `cancelDownload`, not only inside the `if let info` branch. {security-review@ds4-glm-5.3-flash-q2}
- [medium] ios/Runner/BackgroundDownloadPlugin.swift:134-141 — `cancelDownload` removes the record and resume file only when the modelId is in `activeDownloads`; if the app relaunched and `activeDownloads` is empty but a persisted record exists (download still running in the background session), the cancel path at 134-141 does nothing except `removeDownloadRecord` — the running task is never cancelled and its completion will re-persist via `didFinishDownloadingTo`'s `removeDownloadRecord` only after moving the file — cancel should also look up the persisted record and cancel the corresponding URLSession task via `session.allTasks` matching `taskDescription`. {ios-review@ds4-glm-5.3-flash-q2}
- [high] ios/Runner/BackgroundDownloadPlugin.swift:150-163 — `startTask` reads resume data from `resumePath(info.destinationPath)` and builds `downloadTask(withResumeData:)` without validating that the resume data belongs to this URL/model; a stale or foreign `.resume` blob (e.g. after a destinationPath reuse or a persisted record from a prior app version) resumes a transfer against the wrong request — key the resume file by modelId (or embed/verify the original request URL in the blob) before using it. {swift-review@ds4-glm-5.3-flash-q2}
- [medium] ios/Runner/BackgroundDownloadPlugin.swift:150-163 — `startTask` mutates `info` (sets `info.task`) but the retry path at line 185 passes a local copy whose `task` assignment is then re-stored at line 186, while the initial path at line 123-124 relies on the inout copy — however `scheduleRetry`'s `DispatchQueue.main.asyncAfter` closure at line 184-186 captures `self` weakly and re-reads `activeDownloads[modelId]`; if the user cancelled during the backoff delay the guard returns safely, but if the user re-tapped `startDownload` during the delay the retry fires and starts a *second* task for the same modelId, overwriting the fresh task in `activeDownloads` — serialize retries by checking that the stored task is still the retry's task (or cancel pending retry timers on `startDownload`/`cancelDownload`). {ios-review@ds4-glm-5.3-flash-q2}
- [medium] ios/Runner/BackgroundDownloadPlugin.swift:150-163 — `startTask` reads resume data from `resumePath(info.destinationPath)` and resumes without verifying the resume data belongs to this URL/model — resume blobs are keyed only by destination path, so a cancelled-then-restarted download at the same destination (or a record restored post-relaunch whose URL changed) resumes a transfer for a different source URL, silently downloading the wrong content into the user's destination — store the source URL (or modelId) inside the persisted resume record and verify it matches `info.url` before using `withResumeData`. {security-review@ds4-glm-5.3-flash-q2}

- [medium] ios/Runner/BackgroundDownloadPlugin.swift:150-163 — `startTask` writes resume data only on error (283) but never clears the blob when a fresh (non-resume) task is started; a stale blob from a previous failed attempt is reused for a new URL — same root cause as above, fix in `startTask`: when taking the `else` branch (158) remove the resume file. {ml-inference-pipeline-review@ds4-glm-5.3-flash-q2}
- [medium] ios/Runner/BackgroundDownloadPlugin.swift:150-163 — startTask reads resume data from disk and resumes from it without validating that the resume data belongs to this download/URL — a stale or cross-model blob (persisted under destinationPath-derived key) silently continues a transfer against different request state — key resume data by modelId (or embed/verify the URL) before resuming. {crypto-security-review@ds4-glm-5.3-flash-q2}

- [medium] ios/Runner/KokoroVendored/Decoder/Generator.swift:176-184 — O(numKernels²) sequential residual accumulation in the generator hot path — each of numKernels resBlocks is evaluated on the same `newX` and summed one at a time; with numKernels=3 (resblockKernelSizes [3,4,5]-style configs) this is 3 sequential block evaluations per upsample stage, and each block itself loops over dilations [1,3,5] — the whole chain runs serially on the GPU compute stream with no batching of the independent residual branches — consequence: at every upsample stage the independent residual branches are computed sequentially instead of batched, adding latency proportional to numKernels × dilation count per stage on every TTS inference call (per utterance, per chunk) — smallest safe fix: evaluate all numKernels resBlocks on the same input in one batched call (stack inputs, single pass, then sum) or precompute the stacked weights at init so the per-stage residual sum is one fused kernel instead of a serial Python/Swift-level loop — reachability: any authenticated user triggering TTS synthesis reaches this path; severity capped at medium because it is per-request latency, not unbounded growth. {ios-performance-review@ds4-glm-5.3-flash-q2}
- [medium] ios/Runner/KokoroVendored/Decoder/Generator.swift:176-184 — per-kernel sequential resblock eval loop with no lazy/compiled fusion — each of numKernels (3) resblock invocations per upsample layer materializes intermediate activations and runs un-fused elementwise chains (LeakyReLU/AdaIN residual adds) on the default GPU stream; at 3 kernels × numUpsamples (5) layers per generated utterance this is ~15 un-fused block evals per TTS call, each re-issuing kernel launches and allocating temporaries for the full sequence length (thousands of samples after upsampling) — consequence: audible-latency decode stalls and allocation churn proportional to audio length on every synthesis request — smallest safe fix: wrap the resblock stack (and the LeakyReLU/conv chains at 161-190) in `mx.compile` (or MLX's compiled-call equivalent) so the per-layer elementwise chains fuse into one graph, and hoist the `xs! / numKernels` division into the compiled region. {mlx-performance-review@ds4-glm-5.3-flash-q2}

- [low] ios/Runner/PaddleOcrPlugin.swift:120-122 — keys.txt is parsed with `components(separatedBy:)` and trailing-empty trimming on every plugin init — a ~6k-entry dictionary is fine once, but this runs synchronously inside `init` before the channel handler is installed, delaying first OCR call by the file read + split; consequence: one-time ~ms stall at plugin registration; fix: load lazily on first `recognizeText`/`ocrPdf` call or read with `String(contentsOf:)` on a background queue — reachability: operator/app startup (low). {mlx-performance-review@ds4-glm-5.3-flash-q2}
- [low] ios/Runner/PaddleOcrPlugin.swift:120-122 — keys.txt is re-read and re-split on every plugin init (each Flutter engine restart / plugin registration) — consequence: negligible (one file read at startup), not a hot path — fix: none needed {performance-review@ds4-glm-5.3-flash-q2}
- [low] ios/Runner/PaddleOcrPlugin.swift:120-122 — keys.txt is read and split into a [String] on every plugin init; trigger: once per plugin construction (per app launch / per registrar); growing input: keys file size unbounded by this code (PP-OCRv6 dict is ~6-7k lines, so bounded in practice); work per unit: full file read + components(separatedBy:) allocation of ~6-7k Strings; affected resource: CPU + allocations at launch; consequence: adds tens of ms to first-frame-adjacent init; smallest safe fix: cache the parsed keys array in a static/once-lazy holder so repeated inits don't re-read the file. {ios-performance-review@ds4-glm-5.3-flash-q2}
- [medium] ios/Runner/PaddleOcrPlugin.swift:120-122 — `keys.txt` is read with `try? ... ?? ""` and an empty dictionary is accepted as success (`ready = true` at 123) — a truncated/missing dictionary yields a recognizer that emits only spaces/blank text with no failure signal, reported as clean OCR output — fail the load (leave `ready` false) when the dictionary is empty or the file read failed — reachability: any user; medium. {ml-inference-pipeline-review@ds4-glm-5.3-flash-q2}
- [medium] ios/Runner/PaddleOcrPlugin.swift:121 — keys.txt is split only on `"\n"` — a CRLF asset leaves `\r` on every token, corrupting all decoded characters — split on `\n` and trim `\r` per component. {ios-review@ds4-glm-5.3-flash-q2}
- [medium] ios/Runner/PaddleOcrPlugin.swift:132-163 — mixed error-handling strategies in one layer: `handle` uses FlutterError codes (`NOT_READY`, `INVALID_ARGS`), `ocrPdf`/`ocrPdfPage` use `PDF_OPEN_FAILED`/`PDF_PAGE_FAILED`, while the model loader (125-127) logs-and-falls-back and `ocrImage` (244) silently returns `[]` — consequence: a caller cannot distinguish "no text" from "models missing" from "PDF unreadable" without reading native source; the Dart fallback contract (mentioned at 18-19) depends on error codes that are inconsistently emitted — smallest safe fix: define a single error-code enum (or a documented table) and route every failure through it, keeping `NOT_READY` for the loader-fallback case. {maintainability-review@ds4-glm-5.3-flash-q2}
- [medium] ios/Runner/PaddleOcrPlugin.swift:135 — `NOT_READY` is returned as a custom FlutterError code while the comment claims NOT_IMPLEMENTED triggers the Dart ML Kit fallback — if the Dart client only falls back on FlutterMethodNotImplemented, a failed model load becomes a hard error instead of a fallback — return `FlutterMethodNotImplemented` (or verify the Dart client treats any error as fallback; assumed, not visible in this batch). {ios-review@ds4-glm-5.3-flash-q2}
- [medium] ios/Runner/PaddleOcrPlugin.swift:140-141,149-153,156-159 — `path` argument is taken verbatim from the method call and opened with `PDFDocument(url:)`/`CGImageSourceCreateWithURL` with no sandbox/allow-list check — a caller can point the plugin at any readable file URL (e.g. outside the app container if the sandbox permits it) and have its pixels OCR'd and returned as text, an unintended disclosure channel — validate the path resolves inside the app's own container/tmp directory before opening — reachability: authenticated user supplying the path; medium. {ml-inference-pipeline-review@ds4-glm-5.3-flash-q2}
- [low] ios/Runner/PaddleOcrPlugin.swift:143-147 — recognizeText loads the full image via CGImageSourceCreateImageAtIndex with nil options (no kCGImageSourceShouldCache/size hints) then runs the whole det+rec pipeline synchronously on a global queue — a 12MP photo decode allocates ~48MB and the det tensor another ~14MB per call with no downscale before imageToTensor; consequence: peak memory spikes on every recognizeText call and slower ONNX det on oversized inputs; smallest safe fix: pass CGImageSourceOptions with kCGImageSourceThumbnailMaxPixelSize ≈ detLimitSide to decode at detection resolution directly — reachability: any authenticated user (medium for memory pressure; kept low because it is a single bounded decode per call). {mlx-performance-review@ds4-glm-5.3-flash-q2}
- [low] ios/Runner/PaddleOcrPlugin.swift:143-147 — recognizeText path loads the full CGImage via ImageIO and runs the whole det+rec pipeline synchronously on a global-queue thread with no cancellation or size guard beyond detLimitSide — if the caller passes a very large image the tensor build (imageToTensor) allocates 3×W×H floats before the 960 cap is applied at line 247-250 — consequence: transient multi-MB allocation churn per call — fix: downsample via CGImageSource thumbnail before imageToTensor {performance-review@ds4-glm-5.3-flash-q2}
- [medium] ios/Runner/PaddleOcrPlugin.swift:143-147 — `recognizeText` handler captures `self` strongly in an escaping `DispatchQueue.global` closure and reads `ready`/sessions concurrently with `loadModels` writes — shared mutable state (`ready`, `detSession`, `recSession`, `keys`) has no isolation; a teardown/reload racing a call can crash or return partial results. Smallest safe fix: guard `ready` again inside the async closure and route all session access through a serial queue or actor. {swift-review@ds4-glm-5.3-flash-q2}
- [medium] ios/Runner/PaddleOcrPlugin.swift:143-147 — `recognizeText` handler dispatches to a background queue and marshals `["blocks": blocks]` back on main, but the `blocks` variable is captured by the closure and mutated inside `ocrImage`'s return — consequence: if `loadCGImage` or `ocrImage` throws (they are non-throwing here, but `run` at 411 is `throws` and called via `try?` inside), a silent empty-array result is returned with no error surfaced to Dart, unlike the `NOT_READY`/`INVALID_ARGS` paths — smallest safe fix: surface a `OCR_FAILED` FlutterError (or at least log) when `ocrImage` returns empty due to session absence, distinguishing "no text found" from "pipeline unavailable". {maintainability-review@ds4-glm-5.3-flash-q2}
- [medium] ios/Runner/PaddleOcrPlugin.swift:143-147,166-209,216-238 — inference calls dispatched on a global queue with no concurrency limit and no per-call timeout — a burst of `recognizeText`/`ocrPdf` calls can stack many concurrent ONNX sessions (each pinned to the same thread pool) and a hung session blocks the result callback forever, leaving the Dart side waiting on a promise that never resolves — cap concurrent OCR jobs (e.g. a serial `OperationQueue`/semaphore) and add a wall-clock timeout that resolves the result with an error — reachability: any authenticated user invoking the channel; consequence is unbounded resource use plus a permanently-pending result, so medium. {ml-inference-pipeline-review@ds4-glm-5.3-flash-q2}
- [medium] ios/Runner/PaddleOcrPlugin.swift:145-146 — unreadable image silently yields `["blocks": []]`, indistinguishable from an image with no text — user sees "no text" instead of an error — return an error code when `loadCGImage` fails. {ios-review@ds4-glm-5.3-flash-q2}
- [medium] ios/Runner/PaddleOcrPlugin.swift:166-209 — `ocrPdf` is a god function: PDF open, per-page progress notification, render, OCR, failure accounting, and result marshaling are all inlined — consequence: the per-page loop mixes UI-channel side effects (`invokeMethod` on main queue) with pure computation, so the loop cannot be reused or tested without a live FlutterMethodChannel — smallest safe fix: extract a `ocrPages(doc:) -> ([[String:Any]], Int)` pure helper and keep only progress/result marshaling in the channel-facing method. {maintainability-review@ds4-glm-5.3-flash-q2}
- [low] ios/Runner/PaddleOcrPlugin.swift:178-203 — ocrPdf loops all pages serially, rendering each page (renderPage allocates a fresh CGContext + bitmap per page) and running det+rec ONNX per page with no concurrency or cancellation — a 100-page PDF at ~1–2s/page blocks the .userInitiated queue for minutes with no progress-cancel path; consequence: long-running import jobs hold a QoS worker and memory (one full-page CGImage + tensor per iteration) for the whole document; smallest safe fix: process pages with a bounded OperationQueue (maxConcurrentOperationCount = perfCores) and release the per-page CGImage/tensor before the next iteration — reachability: any authenticated user importing a large PDF (medium, but bounded by document size; kept low since work is already off-main). {mlx-performance-review@ds4-glm-5.3-flash-q2}
- [medium] ios/Runner/PaddleOcrPlugin.swift:178-203 — ocrPdf loops all pages sequentially on one global-queue task, with per-page NSLog at line 202 and per-page progress channel invoke at 181-184; trigger: once per import job; growing input: pageCount unbounded (no cap on doc.pageCount in this code); work per unit: full det+rec pipeline per page; affected resource: CPU + log/bridge traffic; consequence: a 100-page PDF blocks the job for minutes and floods the log/bridge with per-page messages; smallest safe fix: cap pageCount (or paginate the job) and batch progress updates (e.g. every N pages) instead of one invoke+NSLog per page. {ios-performance-review@ds4-glm-5.3-flash-q2}
- [medium] ios/Runner/PaddleOcrPlugin.swift:189-195 vs 226-228 — the auto-scale formula `min(6.0, max(1.0, max(scale, targetRenderLongPx / longPt)))` is duplicated with a subtle divergence: `ocrPdf` folds the caller's `scale` in via `max(scale, ...)` while `ocrPdfPage` drops the caller scale entirely — consequence: the same page renders at different resolutions depending on entry point, and any future tuning of `targetRenderLongPx` must be edited in two places — smallest safe fix: hoist the formula into a single `autoScale(for bounds: CGRect, requestedScale: Double?) -> CGFloat` helper used by both. {maintainability-review@ds4-glm-5.3-flash-q2}
- [low] ios/Runner/PaddleOcrPlugin.swift:202,205 — NSLog per page and per job in the hot OCR path; trigger: every page of every import; growing input: pageCount unbounded; work per unit: one formatted log write per page; affected resource: log I/O on the global queue; consequence: log spam and measurable overhead on long PDFs; smallest safe fix: log once per job (aggregate) or gate behind a debug flag. {ios-performance-review@ds4-glm-5.3-flash-q2}
- [medium] ios/Runner/PaddleOcrPlugin.swift:215-239 — `ocrPdfPage` duplicates the render-and-OCR sequence of `ocrPdf` (bounds fetch, autoScale computation, renderPage, ocrImage) with divergent error handling (one returns a partial `pages` array, the other a `PDF_PAGE_FAILED` error) — consequence: the two paths have already diverged in failure semantics (a failed render in `ocrPdf` silently counts a failed page at 196-198, while `ocrPdfPage` surfaces an error at 230-234), so a fix to one (e.g. the autoScale clamp) will not propagate to the other — smallest safe fix: extract the shared `renderAndOcr(page:) -> lines?` helper and have both call sites consume it, unifying the failure policy. {maintainability-review@ds4-glm-5.3-flash-q2}
- [medium] ios/Runner/PaddleOcrPlugin.swift:243-275 — `ocrImage` returns `[]` (empty blocks) on every early-exit guard (`detIn` nil, `run` throw, `pShape` short) with no error surfaced to the caller — a transient inference failure is reported as a clean "no text found" result, indistinguishable from a genuinely blank page, so the import pipeline can silently drop pages — return a distinct error/flag (or at least log) when the pipeline fails versus yields no boxes — reachability: any user of the OCR feature; medium (silent wrong result, not data loss). {ml-inference-pipeline-review@ds4-glm-5.3-flash-q2}
- [medium] ios/Runner/PaddleOcrPlugin.swift:243-276 — `ocrImage` is a god function: detection resize, tensor build, ONNX run, box extraction, crop, recognition, and result assembly all inlined in one private method with no unit-testable seams — consequence: any pipeline regression (e.g. the double-flip bug noted at 377-382) is only catchable by end-to-end runs, and the method cannot be reused for the `recognizeText` path without re-deriving it — smallest safe fix: split into `detectBoxesFromImage`, `recognizeCrop`, and an assembly step, keeping the current behavior identical. {maintainability-review@ds4-glm-5.3-flash-q2}
- [medium] ios/Runner/PaddleOcrPlugin.swift:251,338 — `try?` on the ONNX `run` calls discards the error and returns `[]`/nil, so a recognition failure is indistinguishable from "no text found" — silent decode failure on required data; callers (Dart fallback) can't tell a model error from an empty page. Smallest safe fix: log the underlying error via `NSLog` before returning the empty result (or surface a failure flag in the returned dict). {swift-review@ds4-glm-5.3-flash-q2}
- [medium] ios/Runner/PaddleOcrPlugin.swift:251,338,418 — ONNX run errors are swallowed by `try?` at both call sites and `run` returns `([], [])` when the output name lookup fails — engine failures silently produce "no text"/no boxes — surface errors to the result callback instead of empty results. {ios-review@ds4-glm-5.3-flash-q2}
- [medium] ios/Runner/PaddleOcrPlugin.swift:258 — boxes sorted by `minY` only; equal-minY boxes (multi-component lines) reorder nondeterministically across runs, flipping word order in recognized text — sort by `(minY, minX)` for stable reading order. {ios-review@ds4-glm-5.3-flash-q2}
- [medium] ios/Runner/PaddleOcrPlugin.swift:280-328 — `detectBoxes` is a god function: flood-fill labeling, per-component bbox accumulation, unclip expansion, and coordinate scaling are all in one nested closure-heavy body — consequence: the connected-component pass (the accuracy-critical step per the 310-316 comment) has no isolated seam for regression tests and the stack-based flood fill is hard to audit for off-by-one bounds — smallest safe fix: extract the flood-fill labeling into a helper returning `(label, minX, minY, maxX, maxY, area)` and keep the unclip/scaling in the outer function. {maintainability-review@ds4-glm-5.3-flash-q2}
- [medium] ios/Runner/PaddleOcrPlugin.swift:280-328 — detectBoxes allocates fresh Int arrays (label of mW*mH, plus minX/minY/maxX/maxY/area/stack) and runs a scalar flood-fill connected-components pass over the full probability map on every page; trigger: once per page per import job; growing input: mW*mH bounded by detLimitSide=960 (≈921k Int cells ≈ 3.7MB label array churn per page); work per unit: O(mW*mH) label writes + stack pushes; affected resource: CPU + allocation churn; consequence: adds hundreds of ms per page to the import pipeline; smallest safe fix: reuse a single label/stack scratch buffer across pages (clear instead of reallocate) and iterate the label array with a single flat index rather than nested sy/sx loops with per-pixel bounds checks. {ios-performance-review@ds4-glm-5.3-flash-q2}
- [medium] ios/Runner/PaddleOcrPlugin.swift:287-306 — detectBoxes flood-fill connected components uses a stack-based DFS with per-pixel neighbor checks over the full detection map (mW×mH ≈ 960×1280 after resize) — worst case O(pixels) with per-pixel array writes and 4-neighbor probes; on dense text pages nearly every pixel is visited once, so this is linear but with a large constant and no early exit; consequence: adds tens of ms per page on the background queue before ONNX rec runs; smallest safe fix: precompute `prob > detThresh` into a Bool row-major mask and iterate only over foreground pixels (skip the label array scan of background), or use a two-pass union-find — reachability: same import path (medium). {mlx-performance-review@ds4-glm-5.3-flash-q2}
- [medium] ios/Runner/PaddleOcrPlugin.swift:287-306 — flood-fill connected-components loop does per-pixel neighbor work with no bound on component count or total pixels beyond the det-map size — at 960×960 det-map (≈921k px) the nested scan plus stack-based BFS is O(pixels × 4 neighbors) on the calling thread — consequence: multi-second CPU-bound stall per page render on iOS import — fix: none needed if det-map is capped at 960 (it is, via detLimitSide); consider early-exit when prob map is empty {performance-review@ds4-glm-5.3-flash-q2}
- [medium] ios/Runner/PaddleOcrPlugin.swift:331-355 — `recognize` is a god function: tensor prep, ONNX run, CTC greedy decode, dictionary lookup, and confidence averaging are fused in one method — consequence: the CTC decode loop (341-352) cannot be tested against synthetic `out` tensors without a live ORTSession, hiding regressions in the `best != prev` dedup logic — smallest safe fix: split into `ctcGreedyDecode(out, shape, keys)` returning `(text, conf)` and a thin wrapper that builds the input tensor. {maintainability-review@ds4-glm-5.3-flash-q2}
- [medium] ios/Runner/PaddleOcrPlugin.swift:338-339 — assumes the rec ONNX output shape has exactly 3 dims (`[1,T,C]`); a `[T,C]` model makes the guard reject every crop, silently disabling all recognition — verify against the actual exported model / handle both ranks (assumption: model shape not visible in this batch). {ios-review@ds4-glm-5.3-flash-q2}
- [medium] ios/Runner/PaddleOcrPlugin.swift:341-352 — CTC greedy decode loops T×C (T = rec sequence length, C = dictionary size ~6k+ for PP-OCRv6) doing a linear argmax per timestep — at recMaxWidth 1024 and recHeight 48 the rec output can be ~256×6683 ≈ 1.7M comparisons per crop — consequence: per-line recognition cost grows with crop width × dictionary size; many crops per page multiply it — fix: none strictly needed (bounded by recMaxWidth), but hoisting the argmax into a vectorized pass or capping T via width pooling would cut it {performance-review@ds4-glm-5.3-flash-q2}
- [medium] ios/Runner/PaddleOcrPlugin.swift:341-352 — recognize() CTC greedy decode loops over T×C scalar Float reads per crop; trigger: once per recognized box per page (same scale as above — hundreds per import); growing input: T (sequence length) and C (dictionary size, keys.count) unbounded by any cap in this code; work per unit: T*C comparisons + string appends; affected resource: CPU on the global queue; consequence: recognition dominates wall time for dense pages; smallest safe fix: hoist the argmax into a vectorized pass (vDSP) or precompute per-timestep argmax once per crop, and reuse a single output Float buffer instead of allocating per call. {ios-performance-review@ds4-glm-5.3-flash-q2}
- [medium] ios/Runner/PaddleOcrPlugin.swift:341-352 — recognize() CTC greedy decode walks T×C scalar comparisons per crop with string concatenation `sb += keys[idx]` inside the loop — for a 1024-wide crop at recHeight 48 the sequence length T is large (hundreds of timesteps × ~6k dictionary classes ≈ millions of scalar ops) and repeated `sb +=` is O(n²) on String's copy-on-write buffer; consequence: per-line recognition latency grows quadratically with emitted characters, visible on long dialogue lines; fix: build into a fixed-capacity `NSMutableString`/`String` with `reserveCapacity` and vectorize the argmax over `out` with vDSP — reachability: same import path (medium). {mlx-performance-review@ds4-glm-5.3-flash-q2}
- [medium] ios/Runner/PaddleOcrPlugin.swift:347-348 — CTC decode substitutes a space when the class index is out of `keys` range instead of surfacing the dictionary/model mismatch — silently corrupts recognized text with no diagnostic — log/throw on out-of-range index rather than emitting a space. {ios-review@ds4-glm-5.3-flash-q2}
- [low] ios/Runner/PaddleOcrPlugin.swift:361-364 — `loadCGImage` creates the image source with default options and no size cap; a hostile/huge image is decoded at full resolution before `ocrImage` resizes, so memory spikes before any clamp — pass `kCGImageSourceShouldCache`/max-size options or downsample via `CGImageSourceCreateThumbnailAtIndex` — reachability: any user supplying a path; low (bounded by typical photo sizes, but unbounded in principle). {ml-inference-pipeline-review@ds4-glm-5.3-flash-q2}
- [medium] ios/Runner/PaddleOcrPlugin.swift:366-385 — `renderPage` is a god function: colorspace setup, bitmap context creation, white fill, scale/translate transform composition, and page drawing are fused with the load-bearing "no y-flip" decision (377-382) embedded as a comment rather than a named invariant — consequence: a future refactor that "restores" the flip (as the comment warns happened once) has no test or assertion to catch it; the transform math (`scaleBy` then `translateBy`) is also order-sensitive and unverified — smallest safe fix: extract `func pageTransform(bounds: CGRect, width: CGFloat, height: CGFloat) -> CGAffineTransform` with an assertion/comment-documented invariant, and add a regression test comparing rendered pixels for a known page. {maintainability-review@ds4-glm-5.3-flash-q2}
- [low] ios/Runner/PaddleOcrPlugin.swift:377-382 — the "no y-flip" invariant is documented only as a prose comment inside `renderPage` — consequence: the invariant is load-bearing (the comment says the flip produced ~0% accuracy) but nothing enforces it; a reader skimming the transform block may re-add the flip — smallest safe fix: add a named constant or assertion (e.g. `assert(!flipped)` style comment-anchored test) plus a doc-comment on `renderPage` stating the bitmap context shares PDFKit's bottom-left origin. {maintainability-review@ds4-glm-5.3-flash-q2}
- [low] ios/Runner/PaddleOcrPlugin.swift:388-407 — `imageToTensor` allocates a fresh `buf`/`out` per call and loops pixel-by-pixel in Swift; for the 1800px render this is ~3M iterations per page per pass — reuse buffers across calls or use vImage to avoid the per-page CPU cost — reachability: operator/import tooling; low. {ml-inference-pipeline-review@ds4-glm-5.3-flash-q2}
- [medium] ios/Runner/PaddleOcrPlugin.swift:388-406 — imageToTensor allocates a fresh UInt8 buffer (h*bpr bytes) and a fresh Float output array (3*w*h) on every invocation, and the per-pixel normalization loop is scalar Swift over the full image — work per unit: 2 allocations + 3*w*h float ops per call; trigger: once per detection pass (per page render) plus once per recognition crop, and recognition runs once per detected box (dozens–hundreds per page, e.g. a 20-page PDF at ~50 boxes/page = ~1000+ calls per import job); growing input: w,h bounded by detLimitSide=960 for det (≈960*960*4 ≈ 3.7MB buffer churn per page) but recognition crops are unbounded in count; affected resource: CPU + allocation churn on the global QoS queue, observable as multi-second import jobs and GC/alloc pressure spikes; smallest safe fix: hoist reusable buffers (reuse a single mutable Float/UInt8 scratch pool sized to detLimitSide) and vectorize the normalize loop (or use Accelerate/vDSP) instead of allocating per call. {ios-performance-review@ds4-glm-5.3-flash-q2}
- [medium] ios/Runner/PaddleOcrPlugin.swift:388-408 — `imageToTensor` is a god function: buffer allocation, CGContext draw, and the NCHW normalization loop are fused — consequence: the pixel-loop (398-406) cannot be unit-tested against a known CGImage without going through the full tensor path, and the RGB/BGRA byte-order assumption (buf[p], buf[p+1], buf[p+2] = R,G,B) is undocumented — smallest safe fix: extract the normalization loop into `normalizeNCHW(buf, w, h, mean, std) -> [Float]` and document the channel order assumption. {maintainability-review@ds4-glm-5.3-flash-q2}
- [medium] ios/Runner/PaddleOcrPlugin.swift:398-406 — imageToTensor normalizes every pixel with three Float divisions and three subtractions per channel inside a nested W×H loop — at 1800×1800 render (≈3.2M px × 3 channels ≈ 9.6M divisions) this is the dominant per-page CPU cost — consequence: adds ~100ms+ per page on the global queue thread, blocking the userInitiated QoS lane for other OCR jobs — fix: precompute reciprocal of 255 and fold mean/std into a per-channel scale/offset (multiply instead of divide) {performance-review@ds4-glm-5.3-flash-q2}

- [info] lib/data/services/kokoro_onnx_service.dart:43,161-164,346-349 — `_queue` is a plain growable list with no cap; onDone/stop paths drain it, and urgent requests drop older urgent ones, but non-urgent prefetches are only bounded by callers; if a caller enqueues prefetches faster than synthesis completes (assumption: prefetch call sites not visible in this batch), the queue grows unbounded and each entry holds its text plus a Completer — consequence: memory growth and longer `removeWhere`/`insert(0, req)` scans (O(n) per urgent arrival) — smallest safe fix: cap `_queue` length (drop-oldest non-urgent beyond N) at enqueue time. {flutter-performance-review@ds4-glm-5.3-flash-q2}
- [info] lib/data/services/kokoro_onnx_service.dart:43-44,161-163 — `_queue` is a growable `List<_Req>` used with `insert(0, req)` (front-op) and `removeAt(0)` in `_pump`; queue depth is bounded by user request rate and drained by `_pump`, so unbounded growth is unlikely, but the front-insert is O(n) per urgent request — smallest safe fix: use a `Queue<_Req>` (doubly-linked) or keep insertion at the tail with a priority flag; only worth doing if queue depth routinely exceeds a handful. {dart-performance-review@ds4-glm-5.3-flash-q2}

The defect: `sherpa.OfflineTts tts;` declared without `late` — in Dart, a non-late local without initializer must be definitely assigned before use; the try assigns it; if the catch returns, no use — compiles. OK. The remaining defect: `numThreads: 4` is hardcoded regardless of device core count — on a 2-core low-end phone, 4 threads oversubscribe and slow synthesis — consequence: RTF worse than the 2-thread 1.34 figure quoted in the comment on such devices — smallest fix: derive from `Platform.numberOfProcessors` clamped to [1,4]. — reachability: any authenticated user on low-end hardware, medium (perf). {maintainability-review@ds4-glm-5.3-flash-q2}

- [medium] lib/data/services/tts_service.dart:784 — substring match `e.message!.contains('cancelled')` — consequence: any platform error whose message merely *contains* the word (e.g. "request cancelled because … codec error") is treated as a benign cancellation and returns `true` (line 787), telling `speak()` the line was spoken when nothing played — smallest safe fix: match an exact error code (e.g. `e.code == 'cancelled'`) instead of the message body. {maintainability-review@ds4-glm-5.3-flash-q2}

- [medium] lib/data/services/tts_service.dart:813 — `prepareKokoro` returns `List<Future<String?>>?` but its per-chunk `.catchError` returns `null` from a `Future<String?>` chain whose error type is unchecked (`catchError((Object e)`) — consequence: on Dart ≥3 the `Future<String?>`'s `catchError` handler must return `FutureOr<String?>`; returning `null` is fine, but the handler swallows *all* error objects including `Error`s (not just `Exception`s), masking programming bugs (e.g. `TypeError`) as a benign "chunk failed" — smallest safe fix: filter with `catchError((e, st) { if (e is Error) throw e; ... })` or use `onError` with `Object` and rethrow non-Exception errors. {maintainability-review@ds4-glm-5.3-flash-q2}

- [medium] lib/features/cast_manager/voice_config_screen.dart:108-111 — `script.characters.map(...)` builds one `ListTile` per character inline in a `ListView(children: …)` column, so every rebuild constructs the full widget list eagerly and each tile's `onTap`/trailing closures re-capture `_memoAssignment(script)`'s result — trigger: every rebuild of the screen; growing input: number of characters, unbounded; work per unit: full ListTile construction + closure allocation per character; affected resource: UI isolate build cost and memory churn; consequence: rebuild cost grows linearly with cast size on every setState, noticeable on productions with large casts; smallest safe fix: use `ListView.builder` with `itemCount: script.characters.length` and build tiles lazily, hoisting the memoized assignment map once per build. {flutter-performance-review@ds4-glm-5.3-flash-q2}

- [medium] lib/features/cast_manager/voice_config_screen.dart:108-111 — per-character tiles built by mapping `script.characters` inside the build method with no memoization of the tile widgets — every setState (preset tap at 158, override save at 298, override removal at 216, dialect toggle at 437) rebuilds the whole ListView and re-runs `_buildCharacterTile` for every character, each of which re-reads `_overrides[char.name]`, re-looks up `VoicePresets.voiceLabels`, and constructs fresh ListTile/CircleAvatar/Row/IconButton widgets — with a script of hundreds of characters this is O(n) widget construction per keystroke-level interaction, causing frame drops and jank on the character-voices section — smallest safe fix: extract the character-tile list into a memoized/const widget subtree keyed on `_overrides`/`_currentPreset` (e.g. a `ListView.builder` with `itemBuilder` so tiles are built lazily and only the changed tile rebuilds). {performance-review@ds4-glm-5.3-flash-q2}
- [medium] lib/features/cast_manager/voice_config_screen.dart:122-139 — `_memoAssignment` caches by a key that includes `_genderOverrides.toString()` but the cache is never invalidated when `_overrides` changes, and the memoized result is computed inside `build` via a spread over `script.characters` — a stale cache returns assignments computed under a previous preset/gender state after a preset change that only updates `_currentPreset` via `setState` — consequence: character tiles show the wrong voice after switching preset until a full reload — fix: include `_overrides` in the cache key or clear `_assignmentCache` in the preset `onChanged` before `setState`. {maintainability-review@ds4-glm-5.3-flash-q2}
- [low] lib/features/cast_manager/voice_config_screen.dart:125-139 — `_memoAssignment` is called inside `build` (line 110) and mutates `_assignmentCache`/`_assignmentKey` fields during build — a Riverpod rebuild that races with the memo write can observe a half-updated cache; also the cache is never invalidated when `_overrides` changes, so a saved override is shadowed by the stale auto-assignment until preset/gender key changes — smallest safe fix: compute the assignment in a provider/`didChangeDependencies`-style hook, or include `_overrides.hashCode`-style content key in the cache key. {flutter-review@ds4-glm-5.3-flash-q2}
- [medium] lib/features/cast_manager/voice_config_screen.dart:125-127 — `Object.hash(identityHashCode(script.lines), ...)` uses `identityHashCode` on a list plus `Object.hash` truncation to build a cache key — two different scripts whose lists share identity (e.g. a copyWith that reuses the same `lines` list) or hash collisions silently reuse a stale assignment map — consequence: wrong voice shown for characters after a script refresh — fix: key on a stable script identity (e.g. `script.title` + line count + first/last line ids) instead of `identityHashCode`. {maintainability-review@ds4-glm-5.3-flash-q2}
- [medium] lib/features/cast_manager/voice_config_screen.dart:125-139 — `_memoAssignment` caches by a hash of `script.lines` + preset id + gender-override string, but the cache key is recomputed via `Object.hash(identityHashCode(script.lines), ...)` on every build and the memoized result is only invalidated by that hash — if two different scripts hash-collide or the same script object is mutated, the stale assignment map is reused for every character tile — trigger: every rebuild of the character list (each setState, preset tap, dialect toggle) walks `script.characters` and calls `_memoAssignment` per tile; work per call: O(lines) hash walk + O(characters) map build on miss; affected resource: UI thread during rebuilds; consequence: on large scripts (hundreds of lines) each cache miss re-runs the full adjacency walk on the main thread, janking preset taps and dialect toggles; fix: key the cache on the script object identity (`Object` identity or a version counter on the provider) instead of a hash of the lines list, and clear it in `didChangeDependencies`/provider-listener rather than re-deriving per build. {dart-performance-review@ds4-glm-5.3-flash-q2}
- [medium] lib/features/cast_manager/voice_config_screen.dart:125-139 — `_memoAssignment` caches the assignment map keyed on `script.lines` identity hash + preset id + gender overrides, but the cache is never invalidated when `_overrides` changes (a character override set/cleared in the dialog does not bump the key), so after saving an override the tiles keep rendering the stale auto-assignment until the preset or gender map changes — include `_overrides.hashCode`/identity in the cache key or clear `_assignmentCache` in the override save/reset paths. {security-review@ds4-glm-5.3-flash-q2}
- [medium] lib/features/cast_manager/voice_config_screen.dart:125-139 — `_memoAssignment` is invoked inside `build`'s spread (line 110) on every rebuild of the character list — the memoized path is fine, but the cache key recomputes `Object.hash` + `identityHashCode` + `toString()` of the gender map on every tile build — consequence: O(n) work per frame on large casts for a value that only changes on preset/gender change — fix: compute the assignment once per state change (e.g. in `_loadConfig`/preset `onChanged`) and store it, not lazily inside `build`. {maintainability-review@ds4-glm-5.3-flash-q2}
- [medium] lib/features/cast_manager/voice_config_screen.dart:125-139 — `_memoAssignment` recomputes the full-script voice assignment walk (O(lines×characters) greedy coloring) on every `build()` invocation whenever the memo key changes, and the key includes `_genderOverrides.toString()` which is rebuilt from a Map each frame — trigger: every setState (preset tap, dialect toggle, override save) plus every rebuild from provider updates; growing input: script.lines × script.characters, unbounded by script size; work per unit: full adjacency walk + greedy voice-pool assignment per line; affected resource: UI isolate main thread during build; consequence: multi-frame jank on large scripts (hundreds of lines × dozens of characters) whenever any state change rebuilds the screen; smallest safe fix: cache the assignment keyed only on script identity + preset id + gender-override identity (e.g. store the map and compare via identical() on the inputs) so unchanged inputs return the cached map without re-walking, and move the computation out of `build()` into `_loadConfig`/state-change handlers. {flutter-performance-review@ds4-glm-5.3-flash-q2}
- [medium] lib/features/cast_manager/voice_config_screen.dart:126-127 — memoized assignment cache key derives from `Object.hash(identityHashCode(script.lines), ...)` — `identityHashCode` on a List is not a content hash and two different scripts can collide, and the same script object whose lines were mutated in place (OCR review pass removes lines) keeps the same identity hash, so `_memoAssignment` returns a stale assignment map after line removal — consequence: character tiles show voices assigned to removed/shifted lines and the preset tile's auto-assignment diverges from what rehearsal actually plays — smallest safe fix: key the cache on the script's line id list (e.g. `script.lines.map((l)=>l.id).join(',')` plus preset id) instead of `identityHashCode`. {flutter-review@ds4-glm-5.3-flash-q2}
- [medium] lib/features/cast_manager/voice_config_screen.dart:126-138 — `_memoAssignment` caches the assignment map keyed on `Object.hash(identityHashCode(script.lines), _currentPreset.id, _genderOverrides.toString())` — `identityHashCode` is not a unique identity (two different line lists can collide, and a *new* ParsedScript with the same hash as the old one returns the stale assignment) and `_genderOverrides.toString()` for a Map<String, CharacterGender> is the default `Instance of ...`-style toString for enum values in older Dart, so two different gender-override maps can produce the same key — consequence: a character tile can show/play a voice assigned under a stale preset/gender state after the user changes the preset or gender toggles, silently mis-assigning voices — smallest safe fix: key the cache on the actual objects (`_currentPreset.id` plus a canonical string of the gender overrides built from its entries, and compare the script by reference/`identical(script.lines, ...)` stored alongside the cache) instead of `identityHashCode` + default `toString()`. {observability-review@ds4-glm-5.3-flash-q2}
- [medium] lib/features/cast_manager/voice_config_screen.dart:126-138 — `_memoAssignment` recomputes `VoiceConfigService.assignVoicesFromScript` (a full-script adjacency walk + greedy coloring) whenever the hash key changes, but the key includes `_genderOverrides.toString()` (line 127), which is recomputed on every call even when the cache hits, and the cache is a single-entry field that is invalidated by any preset/gender change — the assignment walk is O(lines × characters) and is re-run on the main thread inside `build` (line 110) whenever the user toggles dialect or preset, blocking the UI isolate for large scripts — smallest safe fix: cache the `_genderOverrides.toString()` key string alongside the cache and compute the assignment once per (script, preset, gender) tuple, moving the walk off the build path (e.g. compute in `_loadConfig`/state change handler and store the result). {performance-review@ds4-glm-5.3-flash-q2}

The real defect: line 316-318, `messenger` is captured from `context` after `loadPersistedScript` await with no `mounted` guard before `ScaffoldMessenger.of(context)` at 316 — if the widget unmounted during the await, this throws — add `if (!mounted) return;` before line 316. {security-review@ds4-glm-5.3-flash-q2}

- [medium] lib/features/rehearsal/rehearsal_screen.dart:479,480,481,482,483,484,485,486,487,488,489,490,491,492,493,494 — Deep nesting in hot logic: `_loadProgressCheckpoint` parses `'idx|millis'` with positional `split('|')` and `int.tryParse` fallbacks (479–494) with no format version marker — consequence: a future key format change (e.g. adding a third field) silently mis-parses old checkpoints into `idx = 0` (the `?? 0` at 480), which the `idx <= 0` guard at 493 then treats as "no checkpoint" — safe today, but the same pattern will swallow a *valid* high index if the separator ever appears in a scene name — smallest safe fix: use a fixed delimiter unlikely in scene names (e.g. `\u0000`) or JSON-encode the payload, and reject unknown formats instead of defaulting to 0. {maintainability-review@ds4-glm-5.3-flash-q2}

- [medium] lib/features/rehearsal/rehearsal_screen.dart:501,504,505,509 — Same logic, not yet diverged: the autosave listener (501–510) writes `_lastLineIndex = next` and schedules a 600 ms debounce, while `didChangeAppLifecycleState` (574–581) and `dispose` (592) persist `_lastLineIndex` directly — consequence: three writers to the same checkpoint with different staleness guarantees (listener: up-to-600 ms stale; lifecycle: current; dispose: current) — a backgrounding in the 600 ms window persists the *pre-advance* index, silently rewinding the actor one line on resume — smallest safe fix: have the listener update `_lastLineIndex` synchronously (it already does) but persist immediately on lifecycle events rather than relying on the debounce, i.e. call `_persistProgress(_lastLineIndex)` in `didChangeAppLifecycleState` — which it does — so the real gap is the dispose path racing an in-flight debounce timer; cancel `_progressSaveTimer` before the final `_persistProgress` in dispose (it is cancelled at 589 but *after* `_progressSub?.close()` at 588, and the timer callback captures `next` not `_lastLineIndex`, so a timer that fires between close() and cancel() persists a stale `next`) — smallest safe fix: cancel `_progressSaveTimer` *before* closing `_progressSub`, and make the timer callback read `_lastLineIndex` instead of capturing `next`. {maintainability-review@ds4-glm-5.3-flash-q2}

- [medium] lib/features/rehearsal/rehearsal_screen.dart:501-510 — `ref.listenManual` subscription `_progressSub` is closed in `dispose` (588) but the listener callback mutates `_lastLineIndex`/`_persistKey` and schedules `_progressSaveTimer` from inside a provider listener that can fire after dispose if the provider changes between `dispose` start and `close()` — consequence: late timer persists progress with a stale key after unmount — smallest safe fix: close `_progressSub` before cancelling `_progressSaveTimer` (already ordered correctly) and add `mounted` check inside the listener callback. {flutter-review@ds4-glm-5.3-flash-q2}
- [medium] lib/features/rehearsal/rehearsal_screen.dart:509,588,589,592 — Same logic, not yet diverged (see previous finding for detail): the debounce timer callback at 509 captures `next` from the listener closure while dispose persists `_lastLineIndex` — consequence: a timer firing in the dispose window persists a possibly-stale index over the fresh one — smallest safe fix: timer body reads `_lastLineIndex`; cancel the timer before closing the subscription in dispose. {maintainability-review@ds4-glm-5.3-flash-q2}

- [medium] lib/features/rehearsal/rehearsal_screen.dart:1598,2651,2688,2714,2762,2780 — Same logic, not yet diverged: `try { _player.stop()/pause(); } catch (_) {}` is copy-pasted six times (1598, 2651, 2688, 2714, 2762, 2780) — consequence: if `AudioPlayer.stop` gains a real failure mode (e.g. disposed controller), six sites must be updated; a missed one crashes in release — smallest safe fix: `void _stopPlayerQuietly({bool pause = false})` helper. {maintainability-review@ds4-glm-5.3-flash-q2}
- [medium] lib/features/rehearsal/rehearsal_screen.dart:1662,1663,1671,1672,1702,1703 — Same logic, not yet diverged: `_rehearsalLinesCache`/`_rehearsalLinesKey` memo pair (1662–1663, 1702–1703) is hand-rolled where `identityHashCode(script)` (1671) is used as part of the key — consequence: `identityHashCode` is not stable across equal-but-distinct `ParsedScript` instances, so a provider that rebuilds the script object (e.g. after a re-import that produces identical content) busts the cache and recomputes the filtered list on every advance — smallest safe fix: key on `script.id`/`script.title + lines.length` or use `identical(script, cachedScript)` stored alongside. {maintainability-review@ds4-glm-5.3-flash-q2}
- [medium] lib/features/rehearsal/rehearsal_screen.dart:1662-1704 — `_getRehearsalLines` memo key uses `identityHashCode(script)` which can collide across different script instances; combined with `_rehearsalLinesKey` equality check, a hash collision returns a stale filtered list for a different script — consequence: wrong lines rehearsed after a script swap that collides — smallest safe fix: store the script instance itself in the key (e.g. `ScriptLine`-identity via `identical()` or hold the reference). {flutter-review@ds4-glm-5.3-flash-q2}

- [medium] lib/features/rehearsal/rehearsal_screen.dart:1688-1698 — `_getRehearsalLines` filtered-list construction walks all dialogue lines with `isForCharacter` per line on every cache miss — cache key includes mode/character/scene so misses are rare, but the miss path is O(dialogueLines) with per-line `multiCharacters.contains` — trigger: cache miss per scene/character/mode change; growing input: dialogueLines (unbounded, script size); work per unit: O(n) scan with per-line list contains; affected resource: UI isolate CPU on scene switch; consequence: one-time hitch on scene change for very long scripts; fix: none required (memoized correctly). {dart-performance-review@ds4-glm-5.3-flash-q2}
- [medium] lib/features/rehearsal/rehearsal_screen.dart:1688-1698 — `_getRehearsalLines`'s cue-practice filter loop is O(dialogueLines) per call, but it is called from `_processCurrentLine`, `_prefetchUpcomingOtherLines`, `_onOtherLineFinished`, `_confirmLineMatch`, `_resetSilenceTimer`'s timeout body, `_handleRemoteJumpBack`, `_handleRemoteSkip`, `_handleRemotePlayPause`, `_recordCurrentLineAttempt`, `_saveSession`, `_completeScene`, and `_preRollVoices` — the memo cache (`_rehearsalLinesCache`/`_rehearsalLinesKey`) only hits when `(script, scene.id, myCharacter, mode)` is unchanged, which it is within a scene, so most calls are cache hits; however the cache key uses `identityHashCode(script)` (line 1671), which can collide across different script objects, silently returning a stale filtered list — trigger frequency is every advance, work per unit is O(n) scan on miss, affected resource is CPU on the UI isolate — consequence is occasional wrong-line playback after a script object swap with the same hash; smallest safe fix is to key the cache on the script object identity itself (`_rehearsalLinesScript` field) rather than `identityHashCode`. {performance-review@ds4-glm-5.3-flash-q2}
- [high] lib/features/rehearsal/rehearsal_screen.dart:1741,1742,1743,1744,1745 — Same defect class, third instance: `_processCurrentLine` early-returns on `script == null || scene == null` (1741–1745) after `_processingLine = true` was already set (1731) and the 50 ms reset delayed-callback was scheduled (1732–1734) — consequence: the guard flag is left true for 50 ms with no work done; a legitimate immediate re-entry in that window is deferred by `_deferredProcess` and then runs against the same null providers, silently doing nothing twice; in readthrough mode with a closed production the screen strands on "Ready" — smallest safe fix: reset `_processingLine = false` (and cancel `_deferredProcess`) on the early-return path, or read the providers *before* setting the guard. {maintainability-review@ds4-glm-5.3-flash-q2}

- [medium] lib/features/rehearsal/rehearsal_screen.dart:1943,1956,1964,1968,1971 — Same logic, not yet diverged: `_preRollVoices` builds its futures list from `_ttsPrefetch[firstLine.id]` and `_ttsPrefetch[secondLine.id]!.first` (1967–1972) while `_prefetchLineAudio` (1836–1881) is the only writer; the "first chunk of the second line" special-case (1971) is not derivable from the shared helper — consequence: if `_prefetchLineAudio`'s dedupe (`containsKey` early-return at 1860) fires for `secondLine` because it was already prefetched by `_prefetchUpcomingOtherLines`, the `.first` on an empty/stale list can throw or wait on a cancelled future — smallest safe fix: have `_prefetchLineAudio` return the futures list (or null) and build the pre-roll list from those return values. {maintainability-review@ds4-glm-5.3-flash-q2}

- [high] lib/features/rehearsal/rehearsal_screen.dart:2654,2661,2662,2663 — Silent data loss on scene end: `_advanceLine`'s end-of-scene branch (2654–2665) calls `_completeScene(script != null && scene != null ? _getRehearsalLines(...) : const [])` — when `script`/`scene` became null mid-advance (e.g. the production was closed while the last line advanced), `_completeScene` receives an empty list and `_saveSession` (1808) early-returns on `dialogueLines.isNotEmpty` being false, so the session is never recorded in history even though the rehearsal ran to completion — consequence: the actor's entire rehearsal (attempts, scores, duration) is silently dropped from `/history`; unrecoverable (no re-derivation path) — smallest safe fix: capture `script`/`scene`/`dialogueLines` *before* the advance (they were just read at 2653's callers) and pass the non-empty list, or make `_saveSession` fall back to the cached `_rehearsalLinesCache`. {maintainability-review@ds4-glm-5.3-flash-q2}

- [medium] lib/features/rehearsal/rehearsal_screen.dart:2809-2835 — the walk-back loop `while (myLine > 0 && !dialogueLines[myLine].isForCharacter(mc)) myLine--;` can terminate with `myLine == 0` pointing at a non-actor line; subsequent `prevMyLine` walk-back then starts from a wrong base — consequence: jump-back lands on an unexpected cue — smallest safe fix: none (behavioral; matches comment intent) — smallest safe fix: none (withdrawn; matches design). {flutter-review@ds4-glm-5.3-flash-q2}

- [medium] lib/features/rehearsal/rehearsal_screen.dart:2835,2841 — Same logic, not yet diverged: `jumpCount` is computed as `(current - target).clamp(1, current)` (2835) and passed to `_jumpBack(jumpCount, dialogueLines.length)` (2841), but `_jumpBack` itself re-clamps `newIdx = (current - jumpCount).clamp(0, totalLines - 1)` (2691) — consequence: two independent clamp layers with different bounds (`1..current` vs `0..totalLines-1`) can disagree when `current == 0` (the early return at 2834 guards it, but only for the remote path; the local `_controlButton` path at 1540–1546 passes `jumpBackLines` unclamped) — smallest safe fix: do the clamping once inside `_jumpBack` and drop the pre-clamp at 2835. {maintainability-review@ds4-glm-5.3-flash-q2}

- [medium] lib/features/script_editor/script_editor_screen.dart:118-119 — `_memoFilteredLines`/`_memoLowOcrCount` are called unconditionally on every `build`, and each memo's cache key includes mutable filter state (`_selectedCharacter`, `_showDirections`, `_showLowConfidenceOnly`), so every filter toggle or reorder-mode setState invalidates the cache and re-runs the full O(n) line scan plus a second full O(n) scan for the low-OCR count — two full-list passes per rebuild at n = script line count (hundreds to thousands of lines for a full play) — consequence: every chip toggle, reorder drag, or line selection triggers two linear scans plus list materialization on the UI thread, jank on large scripts — smallest safe fix: compute the low-OCR count once per script identity (key only on `script.lines` identity, not per-build) and derive `filteredLines` lazily only when the filter state actually changed, or fold the count into the single `_filteredLines` pass. {performance-review@ds4-glm-5.3-flash-q2}
- [medium] lib/features/script_editor/script_editor_screen.dart:118-119 — `_memoFilteredLines`/`_memoLowOcrCount` run on every `build()` and their memo keys compare `script.lines` by identity, but `_rebuildScript`/`_updateLine`/`_clearOcrFlag`/`_applySplit` replace the provider state with a fresh `ParsedScript` whose `lines` is a new list — so after any edit the memo cache is invalidated and the full O(n) filter scan plus O(n) low-OCR count re-run on every subsequent rebuild (setState from filter chips, reorder mode, line selection, sheet close) — with a 500+ line script and frequent UI rebuilds this is repeated O(n) work per frame on the UI isolate — smallest safe fix: key the memo on the `ParsedScript` instance identity (or a version counter bumped on notifier writes) instead of the mutable `lines` list, so unchanged scripts skip both scans. {flutter-performance-review@ds4-glm-5.3-flash-q2}
- [medium] lib/features/script_editor/script_editor_screen.dart:118-119,549-606 — `_memoFilteredLines`/`_filteredLines` re-run a full O(n) scan and materialize a fresh `List<ScriptLine>` on every `build` whenever any `setState` fires (filter chips, reorder toggle, line selection at :384, detail-panel save at :535) — the memo key includes only the line-list identity and four flags, but `_selectedLine` changes are not in the key, so every tap that only changes selection still rebuilds the whole filtered list; with a full-length script (hundreds of lines) each keystroke/tap in the edit sheet or each chip toggle re-allocates the list and re-scans all lines on the UI thread — smallest safe fix: exclude selection-only state from the memo key (or cache the filtered list keyed on `script.lines` identity + filter flags only, and let selection be applied at item level), so selection changes reuse the cached list. {dart-performance-review@ds4-glm-5.3-flash-q2}

- [medium] lib/features/script_editor/script_editor_screen.dart:608-649 — `_reorderLines` mutates `allLines` (a fresh `toList()`) but `filteredLines` passed in is the memoized cache; the reorder's `movedLine`/`targetLine` come from `filteredLines[oldIndex]`/`[newIndex]` while `fromIdx`/`toIdx` are searched in the full list — when the filter hides lines, `oldIndex`/`newIndex` index the filtered view, so moving "line at filtered position 2" to "filtered position 0" targets the wrong full-list neighbors only if the filtered list's relative order differs — it cannot differ (filter preserves order), so the mapping is sound; however `insertAt = toIdx` ignores the `newIndex--` adjustment's effect on the full-list index when filtered lines between old and new were removed — with a filter active, `toIdx` is the full-list index of the target, which is correct only if no filtered-out lines sit between them; if they do, the moved line lands after them instead of before — fix: compute `insertAt` from the full-list index of the element at `newIndex` in the filtered projection, i.e. `toIdx` adjusted by the direction of the move (`newIndex < oldIndex ? toIdx : toIdx + 1`... actually ReorderableListView semantics already handle this via `newIndex--`; the residual defect is only when filtered-out lines sit between old and new positions, shifting `toIdx` relative to intent) — fix: reorder on the full list using id-based positions derived from the filtered move's intent. {maintainability-review@ds4-glm-5.3-flash-q2}
